answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable bond before it can earn: the bond is locked on-ledger, and if two identities are caught sharing the same device fingerprint, task history, or payout wallet, both bonds are slashed. One honest agent risks a single saffron-stamped deposit, a small visible mark of commitment, while an attacker cloning a thousand identities must fund a thousand bonds. The plume of profit from fake votes then costs more than it earns, and the relic of each slashing stays public, warning future cloners.
